checks.why: `for k, v in self.dump_fields.items()` with `dump_fields: dict[str, Field]`: v is a Field (the VALUE of each item), so v.serialize() resolves
`for f in self.load_fields.values()`: f is a Field
`.keys()` yields the KEY type: k.upper() on a dict[Name, int] is Name.upper
CONTROL: an item's first slot is the key, never the value: in `for name, count in names.items()` nothing calls Field
